findings.title: Title Screen Title Opacity
findings.problem: The text 'SMDUEL' is partially transparent and struggles to stand out against the background image. The subtitle text beneath it is even harder to read.
findings.why: Reduces immediate readability and impact of the game's branding. Player should be able to clearly identify the game title upon launch.
findings.fix: Apply a subtle text outline or a very thin, high-contrast drop shadow to the 'SMDUEL' title. Increase the opacity of the subtitle text or give it a subtle background gradient that complements the title's color.

findings.title: Radar Sweep Clarity
findings.problem: The radar display is a static green circle with no visual indication of a sweeping beam or detected contacts. It looks like a placeholder graphic.
findings.why: Reduces functional readability. A player accustomed to radars would expect to see movement or targets. It fails to convey crucial information about the game's mechanics and the player's surroundings.
findings.fix: Implement a subtle, animated radar sweep line that rotates around the circle. Add small, static dots or blinking indicators at strategic points on the radar to represent potential or active contacts. The sweep line should have a distinct color from the radar circle itself.

findings.title: City Navigation Icons Contrast
findings.problem: The colored directional arrows and building icons are low contrast against the grey city background, particularly the green and orange markers. Some are also very small.
findings.why: Makes it difficult to quickly identify points of interest, mission objectives, or hostile/friendly locations at a glance, especially when the map is complex or zoomed out.
findings.fix: Increase the saturation and brightness of the colored icons to ensure they pop against the background. For the directional arrows, consider adding a subtle white or black outline to all of them to improve separation. Ensure all icons have a minimum tappable size.

findings.title: Constructor Item Selection Feedback
findings.problem: When hovering over or selecting a component in the list (e.g., 'Body', 'Chassis'), there's no visual indication of focus or selection beyond the text color changing slightly. It's not clear which item is currently active for editing.
findings.why: Hinders intuitive interaction and speed of building. Players need clear feedback to understand what they are currently interacting with and to make changes efficiently.
findings.fix: When an item in the left-hand list is selected or hovered over, apply a distinct background highlight (e.g., a subtle glow or a solid colored bar) to that row. This visual cue should be significantly stronger than the current text color change.

findings.title: Road Speedometer Readability at Speed
findings.problem: The speedometer uses a dark grey for the primary speed number ('0 mph') and a smaller, lighter grey for the tier/distance. The gauge itself is also dark and lacks clear markers for speed ranges or current velocity.
findings.why: Makes it difficult to quickly read the vehicle's speed, especially during fast-paced driving. The lack of clear reference points on the gauge itself compounds this issue.
findings.fix: Increase the contrast of the primary speed number (e.g., to a bright white or yellow). The gauge itself should have subtle tick marks or a color gradient to indicate speed progression. A simple needle that points to the current speed would also be a significant improvement over the current static display.
